news.title: Malawi FA chief backs Infantino, credits FIFA investment for World Cup breakthrough
news.lede: FILE PHOTO: FIFA President Gianni Infantino attends the inauguration of Abelardo De La Espriella as Colombia's president, in Cali, Colombia, August 7, 2026. REUTERS/Luisa Gonzalez/File Photo. RABAT, Aug 12 - Malawi's qualification for the 2027 Women's World Cup is a result of investment in African football made by FIFA under President Gianni Infantino and why he will likely enjoy the support of the continent, the country's football association President Fleetwood Haiya told Reuters. Malawi have been the surprise package of the ongoing Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) in Morocco, and earned their World Cup berth by reaching the semi-finals.

news.title: Lionel Messi has ‘quite a few doubts’ about football future after death of his father
news.lede: Messi’s father, ⁠Jorge, died last week at age of 68. Argentinian suggests he may not play on much longer. Lionel Messi said on Wednesday that he is having doubts about continuing his career following the death of his father last week. Messi’s father, ⁠Jorge, died last week aged 68 at a medical clinic in the Argentinian city of Rosario after a long illness.

news.title: Messi says not certain to play ‘much longer’ after father’s death
news.lede: Argentina superstar and inspiration behind his country’s 2022 World Cup victory, Lionel Messi, said on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) he has “serious doubts” about continuing to play football for “much longer” after the death of his father Jorge Messi. “I don’t know what I’ll do without you, I don’t know how to go on. I just played football, and now I have serious doubts about continuing to do so for much longer,” Messi, 39, wrote in a message on social media after his father, who was also his agent, died last week aged 68. In the message, Messi, whose contract with Major League Soccer outfit Inter Miami runs till the end of the 2028 season, reflected on the final months of his father’s life, which coincided with the 2026 World Cup.

news.title: 'I wanted to win another World Cup, I coudn't': Lionel Messi pens emotional post after father's demise
news.lede: For the first time since the death of his father Jorge Messi earlier this month, Lionel Messi has spoken publicly, sharing an emotional tribute that offered a deeply personal look at the grief he has been carrying throughout one of the most difficult periods of his life. The Argentina captain posted a photograph with his father alongside the simple caption, "Te amo, pa" ("I love you, Dad"), before accompanying it with a heartfelt letter reflecting on their relationship, the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and the uncertainty he now feels about life without the man who had been beside him since the very beginning." news.title: Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death
news.lede: Jorge Messi watched his son Lionel Messi lead Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup. Lionel Messi said he is unsure how much longer he will continue playing football as he posted an emotional tribute after his father's death. Messi's father Jorge was 68 when he died last week following a long illness. Jorge had been the Argentina forward's agent since he was 14 and watched him become one of the sport's greatest ever players.

news.title: South Korea football crisis: KFA apologises over sexual favours for referees as scandal deepens
news.lede: South Korea's football association is facing enormous scrutiny over a variety of scandals. South Korea's football association has apologised for "various controversies" including a scandal surrounding alleged payments made for sexual favours for foreign referees. A report by the nation's ministry of culture, sport and tourism regarding the allegations was compiled in 2016 and made public last week after it was obtained by South Korean media organisation JTBC. According to JTBC's investigation, the ministry found payments totalling 5.6m won (£2,927) were made using Korea Football Association (KFA) credit cards for "sexual entertainment" at massage parlours for foreign referees visiting the country to officiate matches in the early 2010s.

news.title: Roberto Martinez 'in talks to become new Netherlands boss' despite World Cup failures with Portugal and Belgium
news.lede: ROBERTO MARTINEZ has held talks over the vacant Netherlands national team job. The former Premier League boss, 53, is available after leaving Portugal following their World Cup exit. Dutch football chiefs are after a new boss as they look to replace Ronald Koeman, who departed after his men lost to Morocco on penalties in the round of 32. According to De Telegraaf, Dutch technical director Nigel de Jong has spoken to Martinez regarding the role.
